data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The team should adopt an existing experiment tracker but enforce a 'Schema-First' contract where no data is logged until a formal schema is defined, while simultaneously running a 'Shadow Mode' period where a disposable script mirrors the formal tool's expected inputs to validate the workflow before full migration.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The team lacks the bandwidth to maintain two parallel tracking systems even for a short 2-week period.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The research domain is so novel that no existing schema language (JSON Schema, Protobuf) can express the required state transitions without significant extension.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The existing tools selected do not support webhook or streaming APIs required for the shadow script to push data in real-time.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Hybrid Validation via Schema Enforcement and Parallel Shadow Execution: This mechanism combines the structural rigor of a predefined schema (preventing unstructured noise) with the flexibility of a disposable script (allowing rapid iteration). The shadow script acts as a causal bridge, testing the 'integration tax' hypothesis by attempting to map novel workflow events to the rigid schema in real-time. If the shadow script fails to map events without excessive hacking, it provides empirical evidence that the existing tool's abstraction leaks, justifying a custom build; if it succeeds, the team migrates to the formal tool with verified data integrity.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
